notes.title: Dwarf Legacy Demo is Live!
notes.content:
reading time: 2 minutes

🛠️ Dwarf Legacy Demo is Here! 🛠️

Greetings, brave Dwarffolk!

I'm thrilled (and a little sleep-deprived) to finally share with you the demo of Dwarf Legacy, a passion project I’ve been forging solo in the depths of code and caffeine. Your adventure begins now and I can’t wait to hear what you think!

⚒️ What’s in the Demo?

The demo includes a hearty chunk of the game to dig into:

👉10 hand-crafted levels designed to challenge, surprise, and occasionally explode
👉23 unique perks to shape your own playstyle, agile climber or bomb-happy berserker? You decide!
👉28 optional challenges for the boldest Dwarves among you. Think you can master them all?
👉Native support for Windows and Linux (Steam Deck included)
👉Playable with keyboard or game controller

💬 Join the Conversation
Your feedback is pure gold to me. Whether it's bugs, balancing thoughts, or just your favorite moment, let me know! I’ll be listening closely and making notes (probably on a napkin). Head straight to Dwarf Legacy Community Hub and share what's on your mind!

🔔 Don’t Miss What’s Next
If you enjoy your time with the demo, please follow the game and add Dwarf Legacy to your wishlist. It’s a huge help for a solo dev like me, and it lets you know when new updates are brewing!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2426280/Dwarf_Legacy

Thank you all for giving this demo a try. Now grab your pickaxe, tighten that beard braid, and dive in!

Glory to the Dwarffolk!
Wulo, Solo Dev of Dwarf Legacy

notes.title: Dwarf Legacy Joins the Steam Ramadan Festival 2025!
notes.content:
Reading Time: 4 minutes

Ramadan Kareem to all players! May this holy month bring peace, joy, and prosperity to you and your loved ones. I invite you to embark on a mystical journey in Dwarf Legacy. I invite you to travel back in time and witness the grandeur of The Mountainhome before it was lost to legend.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45102614/6946c60cc5b420db64cc74ae1dd116775b1dcb4c.png

Story of The Mountainhome

Hundreds of years ago, The Mountainhome was the heart of Dwarven civilization, a majestic mountain fortress echoing with life and laughter. It was ruled by The Dwarven King, a wise and just ruler whose leadership brought prosperity to his kin. Under his reign, the forges never grew cold, and the golden halls were adorned with the finest craftsmanship.

During Ramadan, the dwarves celebrated in their own unique way, lighting the great lanterns of the mountain to symbolize hope and unity. The halls shimmered with warmth as families gathered, feasting and sharing tales of heroism and faith. In this golden age, The Mountainhome stood as a beacon of strength and harmony.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45102614/103c272e8ef323378bbe57ece2f2c49de22d415a.png

But shadows loomed on the horizon. The King received visions of an ancient curse looming atop the highest grounds. Determined to protect his people, he ventured to climb the highest peak, facing trials of the mind and heart. Guided by faith and wisdom, he managed to reach the top, but never returned. 

Without The King's wisdom and leadership, The Mountainhome began to crumble. Rival factions fought for power, and fear spread through the once-prosperous halls. The golden lanterns dimmed, and the echoes of laughter were replaced by whispers of sorrow. One by one, the dwarves abandoned their home, leaving behind their greatest treasure.

But the story does not end there. Now, it’s your turn.

The ancient halls of The Mountainhome await a hero brave enough to face the shadows and reclaim the lost legacy. Venture into the long-abandoned mountain, and restore The Mountainhome to its former glory. The echoes of the past call out to you. will you answer?

Ramadan Mubarak!
May your days be filled with peace, and your nights with reflection.

Add Dwarf Legacy to your Wishlist and prepare yourself for a difficult, but noble adventure!


Wulo, Solo Dev of Dwarf Legacy

notes.title: Dev Log 1: Movement and Aiming
notes.content:
Reading time: 3 min

When developing Dwarf Legacy, I wanted every aspect of the game to emphasize precision platforming. The shooting mechanic was no exception. Traditional twin-stick controls divide player's attention between aiming at a distant point and managing their character's movement. This approach didn’t work for my game, as players needed to focus on the hazards directly surrounding the character. This challenge led me to rethink and prototype a new system.

Introducing Weapons
Playing the game without any weaponry, I found the most enjoyment in avoiding danger, jumping away from swarms of enemies, circling around them, and progressing through levels while keeping threats at bay. Once I mastered the movement mechanics, it felt natural to position the character relative to enemies: to the left, right, above, below, or at diagonal angles. This inspired the idea of limiting aiming to predefined directions.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45102614/5c7855e8d2c1ea6512777aafa5390a1976244638.gif

Instead of free aiming, I clamped the shooting angles to the nearest 45° increments based on the right stick’s position. If the right stick wasn’t used, bullets would always fire straight up. This system felt intuitive until I introduced multiple bullets.

The Multiple Bullets Issue
I loved the concept of firing bullets in multiple directions simultaneously. Initially, I implemented a system where one bullet was always fired straight up while the second followed the right stick’s input. However, this design was frustrating. Players often felt like they were wasting the upward bullet, especially when trying to aim precisely. Additionally, circling around enemy swarms became cumbersome, as players had to continuously adjust the right stick to track enemies. This friction led me to abandon the right stick altogether.

Position-Defined Aiming
To me, movement and positioning are the most compelling aspects of precision platformers. This sparked a new idea: what if aiming was entirely tied to the character's position and state? Shooting could then be simplified to a single button press.

In Dwarf Legacy, the character exists in one of three states:
[olist]
 Standing on the Ground
 Hanging on a Wall
 Flying in the Air
[/olist]
I designed the aiming directions based on these states. Here’s how it works with a two-bullet upgrade:
[olist]
 On the Ground: Both bullets fire upward.
 On the Wall: One bullet fires toward the level, and the other fires diagonally upward.
 In the Air: One bullet fires upward, and the other fires downward.
[/olist]
Here is how it looks in motion:

Shooting From the Ground
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45102614/5a5cc4e7e8525066894bfa57a381060649f163b1.gif

Shooting From the Wall
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45102614/1dd0c4859deeb34fe3e045605b18ddadd4c2a7fb.gif

Shooting In the Air
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45102614/4b1cb11dda240e7b375426ed9f1a335e9da3e9ac.gif

Future of This Feature
Simplified aiming has significantly improved Dwarf Legacy. It’s intuitive, enhances the core precision-platforming mechanics, and allows for additional bullets amount upgrades by adding new directions to the predefined states. Additionally, I’ve designed some enemy AI to benefit from these mechanics. For instance, enemies often hover diagonally from players, making them easier targets when the character is hanging on a wall.

Free Demo Coming Soon
A free demo is coming soon to Steam, where you’ll be able to experience this feature firsthand. I’m excited to see how players adapt to and enjoy the refined aiming system. Wishlist Dwarf Legacy Now!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2426280

See you in The Mountainhome!
Wulo, Solo Dev of Dwarf Legacy

notes.title: 200 Wishlists!
notes.content:
First, to the 9gag Community

I just wanted to take a moment to express my deepest gratitude for your incredible response and overwhelming support for Dwarf Legacy! Seeing the community come together with such enthusiasm, especially with over 200 wishlists. 1000 comments and an amazing 14 000 upvotes, gave me a huge boost in motivation. Your feedback, excitement, and engagement are fueling my passion for making this game something truly special.

I am beyond thrilled to have you all on this journey, and I promise to keep you updated every step of the way. From behind-the-scenes insights to progress updates, you'll be the first to know how Dwarf Legacy is evolving thanks to your support.

Thank you again for being part of this adventure. You’ve truly made a difference!

Your feedback

I listen to your feedback all the time. That's why I went through every single comment left by all of you and compiled them. In your comments you mentioned:

ːDwarvenBatː ːDwarvenBatː ːDwarvenBatː ːDwarvenBatː ːDwarvenBatː ːDwarvenBatː 27 times - reference to Galaga/Space Invaders,
ːDwarvenBatː ːDwarvenBatː ːDwarvenBatː ːDwarvenBatː ːDwarvenDynamiteː ːDwarvenDynamiteː 18 times - that the game looks too stressful,
ːDwarvenBatː ːDwarvenBatː ːDwarvenBatː ːDwarvenDynamiteː ːDwarvenDynamiteː ːDwarvenDynamiteː  14 times - that the screenshake annoys you,
ːDwarvenBatː ːDwarvenBatː ːDwarvenDynamiteː ːDwarvenDynamiteː ːDwarvenDynamiteː ːDwarvenDynamiteː 7 times - that the dynamite is over powered,
ːDwarvenBatː ːDwarvenBatː ːDwarvenDynamiteː ːDwarvenDynamiteː ːDwarvenDynamiteː ːDwarvenDynamiteː 5 times - noticed the falling hat animation,
ːDwarvenBatː ːDwarvenDynamiteː ːDwarvenDynamiteː ːDwarvenDynamiteː ːDwarvenDynamiteː ːDwarvenDynamiteː 4 times - mentioned that you like the lighting,
ːDwarvenBatː ːDwarvenDynamiteː ːDwarvenDynamiteː ːDwarvenDynamiteː ːDwarvenDynamiteː ːDwarvenDynamiteː 4 times - wanted to see darker corpses of enemies,

and plenty more...

Your input is incredibly important to me, and I’m committed to making sure all these points will be addressed to create the best possible experience for everyone.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45102614/6220c5ec2eb0a4fed6643e277d6676edf27a6ad7.png

The future

Right now, my main goal is to create the first official gameplay trailer for the game! I know many of you are eager to see more, and I can’t wait to show you what I have been working on. This trailer will give you a first look at the gameplay, mechanics, and some of the exciting features that are coming together. I’ll be working hard to make sure it captures the essence of what Dwarf Legacy is all about.

As all of this unfolds, I’ll be sharing updates with you from time to time. The first will be about the unique way I’ve implemented the aiming controls, which sets Dwarf Legacy apart from other platformers. I’ll dive into that in the next announcement—so stay tuned!

Cheers to you! 
Wulo
